en: Mayon Volcano's steep slopes channel deadly pyroclastic flows rapidly downhill, so residents must evacuate immediately during eruptions.
Coastal provinces facing the Philippine Trench, like Surigao del Sur, must prepare for tsunamis after strong underwater earthquakes.
The Sierra Madre mountain range blocks strong typhoons from the Pacific Ocean, reducing wind damage for inland Luzon communities.
Drinking untreated water from the polluted Pasig River can cause severe waterborne diseases like cholera and leptospirosis.
Stagnant water in discarded tires around Manila creates breeding grounds for Aedes aegypti mosquitoes that carry dengue fever.
Tuguegarao City frequently records the highest heat index in the Philippines, so students must drink water to avoid heatstroke.
Building houses on the steep, loose volcanic soils of Taal Volcano's slopes increases the risk of deadly landslides.
Swimmers on the western beaches of Palawan must watch for strong rip currents that can quickly pull them away from shore.
Heavy vehicle traffic in Metro Manila causes high smog levels, which can trigger asthma attacks in children.
Living in the low-lying coastal plains of Pampanga makes communities highly vulnerable to severe flooding during heavy monsoon rains.
Exploring the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park requires a helmet and a licensed guide to safely navigate the dark caves.
The intense equatorial sunlight in Zamboanga City requires wearing sunscreen to prevent severe sunburns and long-term skin damage.
